articles.title: Messi scam: Governor sanctions prosecution of former minister V Abdurahiman, fresh setback for Pinarayi Vijayan
articles.description: Keralam Governor Om Prakash Mathur gave consent, on November 12, to prosecute former Sports Minister V. Abdurahiman under the Prevention of Corruption Act (PCA), 1988. The decision allows investigators to officially name him as an accused in a sponsorship fraud case tied to the aborted Keralam visit of Lionel Messi and the Argentina national football team. The former minister will now be an accused in the case under the PCA, 1988. The Governor’s action is based on a letter that Chief Minister V.D. Satheeshan forwarded to Governor Om Prakash Mathur. The CM forwarded the letter based on the report submitted by the Special Investigation Team (SIT), led by ADGP (Additional Director General of Police) P. Vijayan IPS. The report recommends prosecution against V. Abdurahiman and four others. The Director General of Prosecution had given legal advice to the government that the Home Ministry could issue a direct order to investigate the corruption charges against the former minister and the officials. Simultaneously, another opinion came from the Department of Law. It said that since the investigation concerned improprieties that occurred while V. Abdurahiman was a minister, the Governor’s consent was necessary for the prosecution proceedings. The SIT had found that there were colossal improprieties and a conspiracy behind awarding the sponsorship contract for bringing football player Lionel Messi and the Argentina team to Keralam. It found that minister V. Abdurahiman had misused his ministerial position by awarding the sponsorship rights to the Reporter Broadcasting Company, the owners of the Reporter TV Malayalam channel, without any sort of tender, thereby helping them make profits. Anto Augustine, the managing director of the Reporter Broadcasting Company, C. Sathyapalan, the former private secretary of V. Abdurahiman, and U. Sharafali, the former president of the Sports Council, are the other accused. The SIT also found that Abdurahiman bypassed official channels and tendering processes to award the sponsorship to the Reporter Broadcasting Company. The probe highlighted financial irregularities, including ₹22.68 crore in unpaid IGST and suspicious overseas fund transfers of ₹126 crore. C. Sathyapalan had given a statement before the Special Investigation Team that the sponsorship was awarded to the Reporter Broadcasting Company in compliance with the minister’s instructions. Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act requires prior sanction to prosecute a public servant for official decisions. Now, with the Governor’s approval in hand, the Special Investigation Team can formally name Abdurahiman as an accused before the Vigilance Court and proceed with further action. Abdurahiman has previously denied the allegations, stating that his actions were intended to bring Lionel Messi and the Argentina football team to Keralam. The controversy concerns alleged financial irregularities in the proposed visit of Lionel Messi and the Argentina national football team to Keralam. The SIT flagged transactions worth ₹549.22 crore, of which ₹336.47 crore remained unexplained, ₹126 crore in overseas transfers and alleged tax evasion of ₹25.78 crore. It also found that Reporter Broadcasting Company secured sponsorship rights without a tender and allegedly submitted forged agreements. The Enforcement Directorate subsequently registered a PMLA case against its managing director, Anto Augustine, widening the investigation into the alleged financial irregularities. V. Abdurahiman was a Cabinet Minister in the CPM-led Left Democratic Front (LDF) government presided over by Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan. He was the Minister for Sports, Minority Affairs and Waqf. Therefore, the latest development is a grave blow to the CPM, LDF and Pinarayi Vijayan.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu saves Rs 116 cr in bicycle purchase after price deal; Hero bags order
articles.description: After facing criticism over the high cost of bicycles proposed for Class 12 students, the State government has renegotiated the procurement price with the lowest bidder, Hero Cycles Ltd, reducing the overall cost by Rs 116.12 crore.
